# Visual Design Reviewer

**Independent decision — APPROVE**

I opened the baseline on port 47831 and the candidate on port 47832 in Chromium at 390 × 844, 900 × 900 and 1440 × 900 in light and pure-black dark themes. I reviewed the paired heading and full-viewport arrival images alongside my live runs. These are my initial findings.

- **Change and improvement.** On “Increasing Disk Space on Linux Servers,” jumping to Conclusion puts the heading well below the top of the viewport because the document ends shortly afterward. The short vertical rule makes the destination identifiable among the table, preceding paragraph, final paragraph and footer. The rule uses the reading gutter. Its right edge is 5 CSS pixels from the text column at all three widths. The rule is 2px wide and grew from about 17.6px high on phone to 22.2px on desktop. The chapter heading, opening paragraph and footer kept their baseline positions. The current desktop Contents row still identifies Conclusion.
- **Typography and hierarchy.** The serif heading retains its weight and contrast throughout. On the Azure Machine Configuration article I also opened the subsection “Uploading ZIP Package to Azure Blob Container.” At 390px it spans two lines. The rule sits alongside the first line, the second returns to the same left edge, and the following PowerShell block starts at the existing spacing. Fenced code computed to TX-02 at 14.5px in both builds. Doubling the root text size left the rule within the gutter, including at 390px where its left edge was 20px. The heading dimensions matched between builds at each enlarged viewport.
- **Color, motion and transitions.** The rust rule on warm off-white and pale tan rule on black distinguish the destination without changing heading ink or placing a fill behind the text. I exercised the inline and desktop Contents, fresh direct fragments, and the Decreasing Disk Space heading permalink. Under ordinary motion the rule was present at arrival and absent after settling. With reduced motion the fresh destination had a static rule in all six viewport/theme combinations. The permalink moved the rule to its own heading.
- **Surroundings and maintainability.** I opened Home and the Blog listing, searched for Azure, moved keyboard selection, dismissed search, opened mobile Explorer and inspected the article header, tables, prose and code. Both builds produced pixel-identical Blog listing and code screenshots in all six comparisons and identical phone Explorer screenshots. The desktop and tablet Home graph rendered on black in ordinary motion. Graph canvases were absent in reduced motion and on phone. The implementation reuses the existing heading rule, theme accent and article router. It adds a decorative child with no footprint in the reading column.
- **Defects and preference.** No demonstrated visual defect or material regression. I have no requested aesthetic revisions.

# Responsive and Accessibility Reviewer

**APPROVE.** The new gutter mark identifies the section reached from Contents or a heading link. It adds a distinct shape at full contrast when the reader arrives, and the heading retains its original ink and line breaks. I found no material or critical accessibility regression and request no correction.

## Independent inspection

I ran the baseline on port 47831 and the candidate on 47832 in Chromium at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels, in light and pure-black themes. I compared the paired arrival, heading, direct-link and context sheets against the live pages. I also ran WebKit on both builds at 390px and the reduced-motion candidate at 320px. Native Chromium tab zoom at 400% produced a 320 × 228 CSS-pixel viewport on both builds. A separate 320 × 844 run covered a tall, narrow viewport. I exercised the Azure and disk articles, a prose link within the Intune article, a cross-article prose link from the Windows AutoRun article to the Acrobat article, Home, Blog, search, the Explorer, code and the graph dialog.

## Findings

- **Keyboard and semantics.** Enter on the inline Contents and right rail navigated to the correct heading. The same link could be activated again and left exactly one mark. Direct loads and both authored prose links produced the same mark. The focus outline remained 2px, focus stayed on the Contents link and subsequent Tab behavior matched baseline. The decoration has no focus stop and is hidden from accessibility APIs. The accessible heading name and level stayed “Increase Disk Space”, level two.
- **Normal motion.** In page-frame samples on the Azure article, the phone heading traveled over 9,000 CSS pixels. It was fully inside the viewport by 967ms and at its final position at 1,500ms, with the mark still at opacity 1. At all three main Chromium widths the settled mark then faded and was removed by approximately 1.90–1.94s. WebKit also showed the accent at arrival and removed it. Only the marker faded. The heading stayed at opacity 1.
- **Reduced motion and forced colors.** Reduced-motion jumps were immediate. The cue had no animation and remained at opacity 1 after 2.2 seconds. Chromium forced-colors produced a black mark on the light canvas and a white mark on the dark canvas. The keyboard outline remained independent.
- **Contrast and typography.** The 2px mark measured 6.31:1 against the warm off-white page and 12.36:1 against pure black. The heading's full ink measured 17.50:1 and 19.26:1 respectively. The heading remained Source Serif 4. Azure's fenced code retained TX-02 at 14.5px in all six width/theme comparisons.
- **Zoom and reflow.** At native 400% zoom the baseline and candidate heading rectangles matched at x=16, y=69.91, width=276 and height=26.84 CSS pixels in both themes. The candidate marker occupied x=9–11, fully inside the gutter. Both documents measured 308 CSS pixels of scroll width in a 320px viewport. The sticky toolbar cleared the heading. The layouts also preserved the cue, text and gutters at 390, 900 and 1440px.
- **Surroundings and navigation.** The first Tab reached Home's skip link, and Enter moved focus to main. Blog listed 56 entries on both builds. ArrowDown selected an Azure result and Escape returned focus to search. Phone Explorer opened by keyboard and returned focus on Escape. Home rendered the graph at tablet and desktop widths, and the global graph opened with focus on Close and restored the trigger on Escape. Phone and reduced-motion contexts suppressed the graph.
- **Maintainability.** The behavior uses an aria-hidden span scoped to article headings, a logical inline border and the existing theme accent. The stylesheet supplies only geometric and motion presentation. Quartz retained its prior focus and scrolling behavior in the exercised flows.

**Defects by severity.** No critical, material or minor regressions observed. I have no preference-only change to request. Keyboard inspection and an accessibility-tree snapshot covered semantics. I did not conduct a spoken screen-reader session.

Evidence includes the paired sheets in `design-evidence/section-cue/` and native zoom and forced-colors captures in `/tmp/quartz-section-cue/`. Independent measurements are in `access-chromium.json`, `access-webkit.json`, `access-zoom.json` and `access-extras.json` in that temporary directory.

# CSS and Quartz V5 review

**APPROVE.** I found no material or critical regression. The indicator adds an arrival cue without changing the section heading’s text, type, measure, or position.

## Scope and evidence

I independently compared the accepted preview on port 47831 with the candidate on port 47832 in Chromium at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels, in light and pure-black dark themes. I also inspected the heading, direct-arrival, full arrival and surrounding-controls screenshot sheets. Tested routes included Home, the Blog listing, Increasing Disk Space on Linux Servers and Setting Up Azure Machine Configuration. I checked the inline Contents, desktop Contents rail, search results and keyboard selection, article code, the Home graph and graph dialog, and page and fragment navigation. All testing used the built site. The graph loaded its archived D3 and Pixi distributions.

## Cascade and integration

- The stylesheet extends the existing article-heading owner in `quartz/styles/custom.scss`. Compiled selector specificity for both geometry rules is (0,2,1). One targets the heading with a direct cue child, the other targets that child. A single namespaced keyframe handles the fade. No new theme tokens, imports, dependencies, breakpoints or global heading state were added.
- In `spa.inline.ts`, the guard requires an HTML heading within the main article’s rendered Markdown and excludes footnotes and popovers. The added span is empty, hidden from assistive technology and ignores pointer events. No authored heading markup, link listener, focus call, secondary scrolling mechanism or additional history entry is required. The existing scroll and history operations still run in their original order.
- At 390, 900 and 1440px, Conclusion retained Source Serif 4 at weight 450 and sizes 22, 24.25 and 27.76px. The heading boxes measured 354.91, 656.5 and 688px wide. The candidate’s cue is 2px wide with 5px of horizontal clearance at the default font size. Azure fenced code used 14.5px TX-02 in both previews at all widths. A direct link in a fresh browser page and clicks on the real visible Contents links marked the requested heading at each width.
- Repeated activation produced exactly one cue. Changing destination moved it to the new heading. Normal motion uses a 1.5s hold and a 0.4s fade, after which the element was absent. Under reduced motion the cue was still present at 2.4s after the click at all three widths. Forced-colors tests resolved the border to the same RGB value as CanvasText in both themes.
- An SPA jump from the disk article to Azure’s Introduction placed one cue on the new heading. Back returned to the prior article and fragment, and Forward restored Azure’s fragment, with zero stale cues after each restoration in both themes. The archive and resting article states contained zero cues. The same search query returned four results in each build and Arrow Down selected the same result. Escape returned focus to Search. The global graph opened a second canvas and Escape returned focus to its opener. Root graph edge inks measured #817d72 and #707070 in both builds. The dark page background computed to pure black.
- Independent checks are recorded in `/tmp/quartz-section-cue/css-audit.json` and `/tmp/quartz-section-cue/css-edge.json`. A separate fresh-page and visible-control run, `css-isolate.cjs`, verified cold loads and reduced-motion persistence on all three layouts. `git diff --check` passed for the source diff.

## Defects and disposition

No demonstrated defect or correction. The submitted implementation meets this review gate. The project-wide automated suite and final acceptance belong to the separate gate owners.

# Design Director decision

**APPROVE** the local section-link cue in `index-81c6d6e2.css` and `postscript-29870e5a.js`. The two-pixel margin rule identifies the heading a reader chose, including at the end of an article where the browser cannot align the heading to the top. Three independent reviewers approved the same candidate. All three completed their reports, and the evidence showed no material regression or disagreement requiring correction.

I compared the published phone, tablet and desktop sheets, including the paired heading, full arrival and surrounding-page views. On the running baseline and candidate I activated Conclusion from inline Contents and the desktop rail using the keyboard at 320, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels. The bounds of the heading and its ink, font and keyboard focus matched at every size. At 320px in dark mode the cue occupied x=9–11 with the heading at x=16. The narrow and tablet reduced-motion cases retained one static mark. The desktop ordinary-motion case showed the mark on arrival and removed it by the settled check. I also confirmed the Azure article's code used TX-02 on both builds. These measurements are in `/tmp/quartz-section-cue/director-spotcheck.json`.

The Visual Design Reviewer verified the first-line alignment beside a wrapped heading, the responsive gutter and the surrounding navigation. The Responsive and Accessibility Reviewer verified 400% native zoom, keyboard and accessibility-tree behavior, forced colors and reduced motion. The CSS and Quartz V5 Reviewer verified the compiled selectors, same-page and cross-article navigation, history traversal and graph behavior. The scoped router change identifies the destination Quartz actually scrolls to. The existing heading rule owns the mark's geometry and appearance. Spoken screen-reader and physical-device sessions were outside the recorded checks.

The production build emitted 913 files, all 164 tests passed, and the changed sources passed formatting and whitespace checks. The generated route, heading, link and table inventories and font files agree with baseline. Browser assertions passed in Chrome, Brave and Firefox. The full repository type check separately returned its two established dependency declaration errors in both builds. I checked that the workflow requiring that full check is upstream-only and this site's deployment workflow requires the production build. The mandatory automated gate passed for this site.

**Disposition.** Accept this candidate locally. The paired images, browser results, build manifest and all three assessments support the decision.
